post.caption:
A dolphin breathes by decision, not reflex, so full sleep would drown it. Its answer is unihemispheric sleep: one hemisphere rests while the other stays alert with that side's eye open, then they swap. Ducks do a version of it, sleeping in a row with the outer birds keeping one eye open. Frigatebirds sleep mid-flight. Giraffes manage about two hours, some bats nineteen. Evolution could have dropped sleep here and instead bent the whole design around keeping it.
